new_statements.quote: Stress is predictable, falling on the third last syllable of a word. For words of three syllables or less, the first syllable is stressed. ju.’u.ba.ae ‘type of taro’ bo.’o.ae.mer ‘grasshopper’
new_statements.citation: SIL [Anonymous; data checked by Pat Lillie and Catherine Easton]. 2011 [document dated 2004]. Organised Phonology Data: Kaian, Kayan Na Yon [KCT], Madang Province. Manuscript, 5 pp. Ukarumpa: SIL. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 42288.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (5 pp., text; the PDF's metadata gives the Author 'Pat Lillie', CreationDate 2004-08-23; extracted text p.4, under the heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)', reads exactly: "Stress is predictable, falling on the third last syllable of a word. For words of three syllables or less, the first syllable is stressed. ju.'u.ba.ae 'type of taro' bo.'o.ae.mer 'grasshopper'" -- verbatim as quoted (only typographic apostrophes differ). Surrounding section: phoneme inventory pp.1-3, diphthongs p.3-4, then Suprasegmentals, Syllable Patterns, phonological/orthographic conventions and a text p.4-5; nothing on tone, contrastive length, secondary stress or exceptions, so 'fixed: antepenultim…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and predictable: it falls on the antepenultimate syllable; in words of three or fewer syllables it falls on the first syllable (which for trisyllables is the antepenult, so effectively antepenultimate stress with initial stress in mono- and disyllables).
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned; no tone or contrastive length reported in the suprasegmentals section.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the word ('third last syllable of a word'); statement based on citation forms in a 5-page SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet; the two illustrative forms are four-syllable words with stress marked before the antepenult.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD describes the speech of Kayan village ('Kaian, Kayan Na Yon [KCT]', Madang Province; population 1010, 2000 census) = Glottolog kaia1245 Kaian, ISO kct; no dialect differentiation. Not to be confused with the Bornean Kayan languages (kaya1333 etc.).
